text:
Maya: quick q — Dedicated tenant used a huge burst and then other keys in the same org were throttled for minutes. we guarantee predictable throughput for reserved pools, right? what's the intended burst + isolation behavior?
Liam: are you seeing that from one API key or across multiple keys in the org?
Maya: single org, multiple keys. looks like one key's batch job drained something and frontends started getting 429s even though GPUs weren't fully saturated.
Chao: that matches the old design: per-key leaky-bucket + a pool-level burst bucket. admission only checks pool burst available, so a noisy key can drain it.
Rachel: customer impact: their background worker annealed burst tokens, then frontend latency spiked and users saw errors. they expected per-tenant fairness within their Dedicated tenant.
Alex: to be explicit: Dedicated semantics we promised: (1) a reserved throughput baseline per-tenant, (2) short bursts allowed but bounded, and (3) tenant isolation so one tenant (or key) can't permanently hog capacity. we need concrete enforcement rules.
Liam: current infra: reserved_tps enforced at admission, burst tokens are global to the cluster pool. admission logic doesn't prefer the tenant's proportional share of burst tokens.
Maya: proposal: allocate burst_tokens_per_tenant proportional to commit and prefer those when their keys ask. Pool-level burst only used when per-tenant buckets exhausted AND most other tenants idle. plus an emergency cap: no tenant can exceed N * reserved_tps for more than M seconds.
Chao: example config suggestion:
```
rate_limit.mode = "dedicated"
reserved_tps = 300
burst_tokens_per_tenant = 600
pool_burst_tokens = 2000
tenant_max_multiplier = 8   # can't exceed 8x reserved for > 30s
tenant_burst_window_s = 30
```
Liam: that seems reasonable. two things to think about: (a) fairness when many tenants need bursts at once — use proportional draining, (b) token refill shaping so noisy neighbors don't permanently starve others.
Rachel: from a support/console perspective we need these signals exposed: per-tenant burst_used, pool_burst_remaining, tenants hitting emergency cap, and an alert when contention is high. also a clear message we can send customers when they opt into the new behavior.
Alex: ops tip: when a tenant hits the emergency cap, try graceful fallback instead of hard 429s — route non-critical/background requests to a lower-priority queue or optionally to hosted fallback if customer's policy permits.
Maya: rollout plan: behind a cluster-level flag (dedicated-burst-fairness). stage to 2 clusters, monitor for 48h, compare latency SLOs and support tickets.
Chao: i'll add stresstests: simulate 100 tenants with patterns: 5% noisy neighbors (long-running batches), 20% spiky web traffic, rest low. we should measure pool_burst_drain_rate, per-tenant burst hit frequency, and tail latency.
Liam: i'll update rate-limiter admission code and add metrics: tenant_burst_ratio, tenant_burst_violation_count. PR once ready.
Maya: can you both post PR link + short summary before EOD? Rachel, can you draft the customer-facing blurb and a support playbook?
Rachel: yup — will prepare a sample message, console copy, and a triage checklist. :thumbsup:
quota-bot: NOTE: config flag "dedicated-burst-fairness" is currently OFF in clusters [eu-1, us-west-2]. use `/quotalist` to inspect current cluster flags.
